finding.claim: authorize() is async but not awaited in the DELETE handler, so the authorization check is ineffective. The report is deleted regardless of the grant result. The rejected promise is unhandled, so it may also crash the process on newer Node versions.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sending DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id

trace.note: authorize(...) called without await; the 403 throw becomes a rejected promise that nothing awaits
db.reports.remove runs immediately, before the grant lookup finishes

finding.guards_checked: The authorize function itself is correct and is awaited in the PUT handler at line 27. The DELETE handler neither awaits it nor attaches a .catch to it. No other middleware does authorization. The only global middleware sets req.user.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it as a bare un-awaited statement at line 20 with no .catch. The only global middleware (lines 4-7) sets req.user and does no authorization.
verdict.reason: The un-awaited authorize() call at server.js:20 lets its 403 throw become an unhandled rejection, so db.reports.remove at server.js:21 and the 204 at line 22 run regardless of the grant, reachable by any authenticated user.

finding.claim: The PUT handler passes the whole client-controlled req.body to db.reports.update, so a user with only the write grant can set any field, such as owner, id or ACL fields (mass assignment). This is plausible but depends on what db.reports.update does with the object, and db is not defined in this file.
finding.source: JSON body of PUT /reports/:id from a user holding the write grant

trace.note: express.json() parses the body into an arbitrary object
authorize checks only the 'write' action on this report
the whole body is passed to update with no field allowlist

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation was found. The authorize call is awaited, so the write grant is enforced. The db implementation is not in the codebase, so the impact is unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 and is awaited at server.js:27, so write grant is enforced; no field allowlist or schema validation on req.body
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (server.js:3, 27, 28) and an authenticated write-grant user can send arbitrary fields in req.body to db.reports.update at server.js:28, but db is undefined in the codebase, so whether it applies owner/id/ACL fields can't be determined.
